title: 12V Battery Runtime Calculator (100Ah to 200Ah) | Wattlyst
meta: Find how long a 12V battery runs your load. Works for 100Ah, 150Ah and 200Ah, lead-acid or lithium, with DC and inverter loads.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: How long will a 12 V battery run a 100 W load?
p: A 100 Ah, 12 V lead-acid battery runs a 100 W AC load for about 4 h 3 min through an inverter. The same load wired as DC, with no inverter, runs longer, because there is no inverter loss (about 85% efficiency) and no idle draw of the inverter itself. A 100 Ah lithium battery at 12.8 V stores about 1,152 Wh usable, so it runs the same 100 W load for roughly twice as long.

The result does not depend on your mains voltage. Whether the inverter puts out 230 V as in Pakistan, the UK and Europe, or 120 V as in the US and Canada, the battery side is the same 12 V and the watts drawn are the same.

sections.h2: 100 Ah battery runtime calculator: lead-acid against lithium
p: The label Ah is not the usable Ah. A 100 Ah lead-acid, AGM or gel battery should only be taken to about 50% of its rating, so only half the energy counts. A 100 Ah lithium (LiFePO4) battery can safely use about 90%, and sits at 12.8 V instead of 12 V, which is why the lithium example below gives about 3 h at 300 W while a lead-acid battery of the same Ah gives much less.

Lead-acid batteries also lose capacity when they are drained fast. The label Ah is measured over about twenty hours; at a load that empties the battery in an hour the real capacity can be a quarter lower. The calculator does not apply this drop, so treat results under about two hours as optimistic.

faq.q: How long will a 12 V battery last?
faq.a: Divide the usable watt-hours by what the inverter takes from the battery: the load watts ÷ its efficiency, plus its own idle draw. A 100 Ah lead-acid battery has about 600 Wh usable, so it lasts about 4 h 3 min at 100 W, about 1 h 56 min at 500 W if it is a 200 Ah battery, and about 29 min at 1,000 W.

faq.q: A 100 Ah battery gives how many hours?
faq.a: About 4 h 3 min at 100 W through an inverter, or about 3 h at 300 W if it is a 12.8 V lithium battery. The hours fall almost in proportion as the load rises.

faq.q: Can a 12 V 100 Ah battery run a 1,000 W load?
faq.a: Only briefly: about 29 min on paper, and less in practice because a lead-acid battery drained that fast delivers less than its label Ah. You also need an inverter rated for the load and a thick, fused battery cable for the high current.

faq.q: Is this a 12 V battery life calculator?
faq.a: It calculates runtime on one charge, not the life of the battery in years. Battery life depends on how deep and how often you discharge; staying within about 50% for lead-acid and about 90% for lithium is what makes a battery last.

faq.q: How long will a 12 V battery run a fridge?
faq.a: Use the fridge's average draw, not its peak. A 12 V compressor fridge averaging about 60 W runs about 10 h on a 100 Ah lead-acid battery wired as DC. A mains fridge through an inverter draws more and also pays the inverter loss.

faq.q: What is the runtime of a 12 V deep cycle battery?
faq.a: The same formula applies; deep cycle batteries are simply built to be taken to about 50% repeatedly. A 200 Ah deep cycle battery runs a 500 W load for about 1 h 56 min through an inverter.

faq.q: How do I work out the discharge time of a 12 V battery?
faq.a: Discharge time in hours = Ah × 12 V × usable depth of discharge ÷ (load watts ÷ inverter efficiency + the inverter's idle draw). For a DC load drop the inverter efficiency and the idle draw; then usable Wh ÷ watts gives the hours and Ah × depth of discharge ÷ amps gives the same answer.

key_facts: Runtime of a 12 V battery in hours = Ah × 12 V × usable depth of discharge ÷ (load watts ÷ inverter efficiency + the inverter's idle draw).
A 100 Ah, 12 V lead-acid battery stores about 600 Wh of usable energy, which through an inverter runs a 100 W load for about 4 h 3 min or a 1,000 W load for about 29 min.
Lead-acid, AGM and gel batteries should be used to about 50% of their rating; lithium (LiFePO4) batteries to about 90%, so a lithium battery of the same Ah runs almost twice as long.

An inverter running at about 85% efficiency turns the rest of the battery energy into heat; the inverter also draws about 30 W itself while it is on. A DC load wired straight to the battery has neither loss.
mistakes: Using the full Ah. A lead-acid battery taken below about 50% loses cycles quickly, so only that part counts as usable.
Forgetting the inverter. An inverter turns about 85% of the battery energy into AC; leave the efficiency at one only for a true DC load.
Using the fridge's peak watts. A fridge compressor cycles on and off; use the average draw over a day or the runtime will look far too short.
Trusting the label Ah at high loads. Lead-acid capacity is rated over about twenty hours; a load that empties the battery in an hour or two gets noticeably less.
Mixing up a car battery with a deep cycle battery. A car starting battery is built for short bursts and is damaged by deep discharge, so set a smaller depth of discharge for it.

fields.name: ah
fields.label: Battery capacity
fields.hint: From the battery label. Common sizes are 100, 150 and 200 Ah.

fields.name: load_w
fields.label: Load
fields.hint: Total watts the battery is powering. For a fridge or cooler use its average draw, not the peak.

fields.name: inverter_eff
fields.label: Inverter efficiency
fields.hint: As a decimal. Enter 1 for a DC load wired straight to the battery.

fields.name: idle_w
fields.label: Inverter idle draw
fields.hint: What the UPS or inverter uses itself, even with nothing plugged in (no-load current × battery volts on its label). Not counted when inverter efficiency is one (a DC load).

fields.name: dod
fields.label: Usable depth of discharge
fields.hint: As a decimal: 0.5 means half the battery. Leave blank to use the value for your battery type.

how.tpl: {{in.ah}} Ah × {{in.volts|1}} V × {{out.dod|pct}} usable = {{out.stored_wh|int}} Wh in the battery. The battery gives {{in.load_w}} W ÷ {{out.inverter_eff|pct}} inverter efficiency + {{out.idle_w}} W the inverter draws itself = {{out.battery_w|1}} W. {{out.stored_wh|int}} Wh ÷ {{out.battery_w|1}} W = {{out.hours|2}} hours, about {{out.hours|hm}}. Battery current: {{out.battery_w|1}} W ÷ {{in.volts|1}} V = {{out.battery_a|1}} A, {{out.c_rate|2}} times the battery's Ah (its C-rate), rising to {{out.cutoff_a|1}} A as the battery nears its low-battery cut-off; the cables and fuse must carry that.
how.text: 100 Ah × 12 V × 50% usable = 600 Wh in the battery. The battery gives 100 W ÷ 85% inverter efficiency + 30 W the inverter draws itself = 147.6 W. 600 Wh ÷ 147.6 W = 4.06 hours, about 4 h 3 min. Battery current: 147.6 W ÷ 12 V = 12.3 A, 0.12 times the battery's Ah (its C-rate), rising to 14.1 A as the battery nears its low-battery cut-off; the cables and fuse must carry that.

msg.load_must_be_positive: Enter a load greater than 0 watts.
msg.bank_voltage_not_multiple_of_battery: The bank voltage must be a whole multiple of the battery voltage (for example 24 V = 2 × 12 V).
msg.n_parallel_must_be_whole: Number of parallel strings must be a whole number.
msg.n_series_must_be_whole: Number of batteries in series must be a whole number.
msg.surge_w_required: Enter the starting (surge) watts of your load, or leave both surge fields blank.
msg.surge_rating_w_required: Enter the UPS surge rating from its label, or leave both surge fields blank.
msg.appliance_unknown: Pick an appliance from the list, or choose Custom and enter its watts.
msg.load_exceeds_ups_rating: This load is more than the UPS can deliver (VA × power factor). Choose a bigger UPS or reduce the load.
msg.surge_exceeds_ups_rating: The starting surge is above the UPS surge rating. Choose a bigger UPS or remove the motor load.
msg.high_c_rate: This load draws a high current for the battery size: a lead-acid battery then gives well under its rated Ah, so the real backup is shorter than shown, and a lithium battery may shut off. Check the battery's maximum discharge current or use a bigger bank.
msg.forecast_unavailable: The live forecast is not available right now, so a typical day is shown. Try again later.
msg.typical_used: Blank boxes in your list use the typical value for that appliance (its listed watts and hours a day, quantity 1). Type your own numbers for an exact result.
msg.internal_non_finite: These numbers are outside a realistic range. Please check your inputs.

examples.title: 100 Ah battery with a 100 W load through an inverter
examples.text: 100 Ah × 12 V × 50% = 600 Wh usable. 600 Wh ÷ 148 W from the battery = about 4 h 3 min.

examples.title: 100 Ah battery with a 1,000 W load (microwave or kettle)
examples.text: The same 600 Wh ÷ 1,206 W from the battery = about 29 min. At this rate the inverter pulls well over eighty amps from the battery, and a lead-acid battery drained this fast gives less than its label Ah, so expect even less in practice.

examples.title: 100 Ah lithium battery with a 300 W load
examples.text: 100 Ah × 12.8 V × 90% = 1,152 Wh usable, which runs 300 W (a TV with a few fans, or a small compressor fridge at full duty) for about 3 h.

examples.title: 12 V compressor fridge, 60 W average, wired as DC
examples.text: A 12 V camping or car fridge draws more when the compressor runs and nothing when it rests; its average over a day is about 60 W. With inverter efficiency set to one: 100 Ah × 12 V × 50% = 600 Wh, ÷ 60 W from the battery = about 10 h.

examples.title: 200 Ah deep cycle battery with a 500 W load
examples.text: 200 Ah × 12 V × 50% = 1,200 Wh usable. 1,200 Wh ÷ 618 W from the battery = about 1 h 56 min.

content.safety: Fuse the battery cable close to the battery, size the cable for the inverter current, keep lead-acid batteries ventilated, and have a licensed electrician connect any inverter to house wiring.
